column1: # Tag audit proposals — tranche 6: every 8th flag by code at offset 5 (32 of 254).
# Additions and aliases; removals are their own round. See #174.
# HOW TO REVIEW: delete the rows you disagree with. What survives is applied.
# Nothing else to fill in; the deletions are themselves the record of your call.
# The pull request shows each flag's image beside its row.
# Then say so, and the agent runs scripts/apply-tag-audit.mjs, the validators and
# the Playwright suite. Do not edit proposals.original.tsv — the difference
# between it and this file is how your rejections get remembered.
# Read the name; the code beside it is what the script applies to, and a row whose
# name and code disagree is refused. To see a flag: https://flagfilter.com/?q=<name>
# Columns: name, code, tag or alias, add|remove|alias, confidence, why.

column6: The white triangle at the hoist carries the star and the bird.
The double cross and the three hills are on a red shield.
The volcanoes, sea and cap are framed by a golden triangle, as in Nicaragua's emblem, which carries triangle.
The sea at the foot of the volcanoes is drawn as wavy blue and white lines, as in Nicaragua's emblem, which carries waves.
The map of the island sits on a yellow disc.
A macaroni penguin supports the shield on the right.
Two gold stars from James Cook's arms are on the shield beside the lion.
A knight's helmet sits on the shield under the reindeer. Headwear, as Andorra's mitre is; it is part of the arms.
The compass is a closed black ring round the red star, a ring like Kyrgyzstan's.
The orange disc is the sun, per the flag's own symbolism. A shape that reads as two things gets both, like Palau's disc.
The palm tree is a plain green emblem on the field, like Barbados's black trident; it is 4% of the flag.
The field is six wavy blue and white horizontal stripes. They are waves, but also a set of parallel stripes plain to see.
The emblem is a black double-headed eagle.
What the emblem is called; the search drops the hyphen in both the alias and the query.
The emblem is a red maple leaf; the vocabulary rules name it as an alias that passes.
The emblem is a gold lion, standing alone on the maroon panel rather than in a shield.
The lion holds a sword in its raised paw.
The red and white checkerboard shield is what the flag is known by.
The word the flag's own symbolism uses for the pattern.
The red and blue taegeuk is what most people take for a yin-yang.
The emblem's name, as the flag's own symbolism gives it.
A palm tree stands on the waves; searching palm matches it too.
The emblem is a curled boar's tusk.
What the emblem is; the search turns the apostrophe into a space.
The same written without the apostrophe, which the first does not match.
What the flag is called; the search reads cross as the filter and matches the rest.
The same without the apostrophe, which the first does not match.
The same with saint written out.
The same, saint written out and no apostrophe.
The emblem is a white double cross; the search reads cross as the filter and matches double.
The black ring with four points is a compass, per the flag's own symbolism.
What the flag is called in Japan, as union jack is for the United Kingdom.
